5 Plates and symbols on vehicles
5.1 Licence plates (Vehicle registration plates/marks)
Vehicle registration plates are comprised of both letters and numbers that serve to identify a particular vehicle, as per the registration documents.
Motor vehicles, except motorcycles, threewheeled vehicles and heavy quadricycles, must carry two registration plates: one at the front and one at the rear.
Mopeds, motorcycles, three-wheeled vehicles, and both light and heavy quadricycles must carry a single registration plate at the rear. Light and heavy quadricycles may also optionally carry a front registration plate, identical in specification to the rear one.
(Página 219 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5.2 Other distinctive plates, symbols, signs and stickers  
5.2.4 Slow vehicle (V-5)
It indicates a motor vehicle, (or set of vehicles) due its design, cannot exceed the speed of 40 kilometres per hour.
(Página 220 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5.2 Other distinctive plates, symbols, signs and stickers  
5.2.5 Long vehicle (V-6)
This plate is placed at the rear of a vehicle to indicate that the vehicle or set of vehicles is longer than 12 metres in length. It is a yellow, reflective rectangular plate framed by a fluorescent red border.
Alternatively, smaller plates may be used and more conveniently located symmetrically on the vehicle.
(Página 220 del manual 'Learning to drive')
